segments.expected: He was standing beside her. Aske had let him come on condition that he did not stand for long, and he had already stood for longer than that. He had his coat buttoned over the linen and his hand pressed to his side. "Ninth," said Kiva. "One mark off eighth. One mark off the roll." He looked at the sheet. "Third last night. Ninth tonight. Fifteenth on the Hunt, with no remarks, with clean work on our stow and a fold called and a pass that held." He was quiet for a moment. "With a dry bag that combed red and a dry bag that combed clean, off the same stow in the same slack, and nobody can say why."
